method: Manual inspection of all 108 cells and native-size six-neighbor contact sheets around the requested four seams. A continuous 224x243 GIF/WebP was assembled from the final registered runtime cells; motion is not judged from file hashes or frame count.

seams.observation: Face/head scale remains close. Eyes open from a closed blink, but crossed feet immediately become parallel feet rather than passing through an uncrossing pose. Foot baseline stays fixed. A small stance reset is visible in the native neighboring cells.

Forward-facing clasped-hands pose and both feet agree. Head crown stays at nearly the same Y. The long hair silhouette contracts at the cut and cape/collar linework changes slightly. The next two frames then extend the arms coherently. No large foot or head-height jump.

The raised-arm general action continues, but the face/veil moves downward and appears smaller while the extended leg switches abruptly to a crossed stance. Closed-eye smile changes to a different open-eye face at the same cut. Integer floor registration removes the old floor-Y change, but it does not remove this drawn head/face/stance discontinuity. Bbox height also changes, partly due to arm and head posture; bbox alone is not a scale measurement.

Both cells are essentially the same neutral standing stance with lowered arms and parallel feet. The return figure has a lower/smaller head and shorter overall standing silhouette. Entry immediately restores a taller head/body drawing, raising the crown about 14 px while the floor stays fixed. This is a visible size/face pop at every loop and cannot be accepted as a seamless repeat.

overall: All cells are populated and the final integer-Y floor registration is effective. The 108-frame sequence has actual changing poses, including the turn, rather than just duplicates. The two major seam issues above remain; no claim that the full loop is already smooth is made.
recommended_action: Keep whole-frame floor registration. Redraw the affected continuation/return families with matching head size and stance, or have the animation owner choose genuinely matching drawn endpoints. Do not fix by individually scaling the character or cross-fading mismatched feet.
scope_limit: This review checks rendered continuity and character proportions. It does not independently re-audit the official OP timecode or claim that 108 cells alone establish dance accuracy.
